reasons: This is a template, so copying it unchanged leaves placeholder values in place.
Several listed settings are not read by the code shown.
Development switches are on by default.

terms.meaning: A named setting passed to a program by the operating system, separate from the code.
An example value that must be replaced with a real one.
A list of approved items. Only matches are allowed when it is not empty.
A browser rule about which web pages may call the server.
Tools for caching and running background jobs. Settings exist here, but the visible code does not use them.
An outside service that collects error reports from running software.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Database, server, security and currency settings
sections.what: Sets the database address (a SQLite file by default), pool sizes, server host, port, worker count, reload and debug flags, token lifetimes and default role, the base quarter and currency, index series names, and the exchange rate service address.
sections.why: Lets operators change where data lives and how the server runs without editing code.
sections.watch_out: SECRET_KEY is a placeholder that must be replaced with a long random value before any real use, and DEBUG is not read by the code shown.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Web research and credibility settings
sections.what: Sets how the crawler behaves (robots rules, user agent, rate, timeouts), the domain allowlist, and the weights and scores that rank how trustworthy a source is.
sections.why: Lets operators tune how strict source checks are without changing code.
sections.watch_out: The four credibility weights should add up to 1, but nothing checks this, so a mismatch shifts every score.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Modeling, schedule and background job settings
sections.what: Sets the minimum comparator count, regression and outlier settings, variance steps, conflict thresholds, schedule simulation counts and seed, solar work-rate defaults, and Redis and Celery addresses.
sections.why: Lets analysts tune cost models and schedule runs.
sections.watch_out: The Redis and Celery settings are not read by the code shown, so changing them probably does nothing yet.

sections.name: File setup (part 4)
sections.title: Logging, storage and feature switch settings
sections.what: Sets the log level, log file, audit log, upload and export folders, file size limit, the presentation template path, location data paths, feature switches, and error monitoring.
sections.why: Lets operators choose where files are kept and which features run.
sections.watch_out: The feature switches are not read by any code in the files shown, so turning them on or off may have no effect.

sections.name: File setup (part 5)
sections.title: Frontend access and development switches
sections.what: Lists the web addresses allowed to call the API from a browser, and development switches for seed data and skipping login.
sections.why: Lets developers work locally without logging in.
sections.watch_out: DEV_SKIP_AUTH and DEV_MODE would bypass protections if enabled on a real server, and the visible code does not read them, so do not rely on them.

summary: A template listing the settings the platform can read, with example values to copy into a real environment file.
purpose: Documents every setting in one place, grouped by topic, so an operator can copy the file and change the values.
why: Likely reason: lets a new user set up the app without reading every code file. The real settings file is meant to be kept separate, which the template suggests but does not state directly.
how: 1. The user copies this file to a real environment file. 2. The user edits values such as the secret key, database address and allowlist. 3. The app reads matching environment variables at startup, through the code that calls os.getenv.
inputs: Read by the person setting up the app, or by a tool that loads environment files. The app reads the matching environment variables.
outputs: Nothing directly. Its values become the settings the app uses.
risks: SECRET_KEY is a placeholder and must be replaced. DEV_MODE is set to true. Many listed settings, such as Redis, Celery, FX_API_KEY, SECRET_KEY and CORS_ORIGINS, are not read by the code shown, so changing them may have no effect. An empty ALLOWLIST_DOMAINS allows all sites.
debug: If a setting seems ignored, search the code for its exact name. If the app behaves in development mode, check DEV_MODE and DEV_SKIP_AUTH. If the database is not where you expect, check DATABASE_URL.
